subject: Compact console lab — seat backfill & timebox request
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@ledgerly.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh@ledgerly.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compact console lab request — availability and headcount

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — the execs liked the throughput numbers. We'd like to schedule a compact "console lab" (console walkthrough + 1-hour API mini-lab) for our product and infra teams. A few constraints from our side:

- Prefer a single, tightly timeboxed session (60–75 minutes).
- 6 attendees (2 PM-level engineers, 2 data/infra, 2 product managers).
- We may need a last-minute seat backfill if someone gets pulled into an incident; what's your policy?
- We need confirmation on environment access and whether we need service account keys pre-provisioned or if a temporary token during the session is OK.

Our preferred windows (Pacific):
- Tue Sept 7, 10:30–11:45am
- Wed Sept 8, 3:00–4:15pm

I've attached our preflight sheet with attendee names and a placeholder calendar invite. Can you confirm which window works and whether Redwood can shorten the agenda to fit 60 minutes if needed?

Appreciate it —
Emma
Emma Li
Director of Engineering, Ledgerly
emma.li@ledgerly.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: ledgerly-preflight-sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet), ledgerly-cal-placeholder.ics (calendar placeholder)
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compact console lab request — availability and headcount

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear constraints and the preflight. Both proposed windows could work. Quick notes and suggestions: 

- We can run a compact format and reliably hit a 60-minute timebox if we trim the hands-on portion to a single API exercise and move some deeper ops topics into a follow-up doc or short recording.
- Seat backfill: yes — we provide one last-minute replacement without additional cost if you give >= 2 hours notice. For true "walk-in" replacements during a live incident we'll prioritize a lightweight observer role vs. full hands-on seat.
- Env/access: fine to use temporary tokens for the session; however, if you want to mirror Ledgerly infra we can provision a scoped service account for the lab. Irene (cc) handles credential provisioning and will confirm the best path.

Proposed plan (short):
1) 10–15m: goals + top-level console tour (we'll highlight routing, model pinning, and cost breakdowns)
2) 30m: single API enablement exercise (generate + KV cache demo)
3) 10–15m: Q&A and next steps (rollouts, billing/quotas)

Options — pick one and we will tighten agenda:
A) Tue Sept 7, 10:30–11:30 PT (60m compact)
B) Wed Sept 8, 15:00–16:00 PT (60m compact)

Ben will run the API exercise and Sofia will handle the console tour. If you confirm a time, we'll send a final invite with roles and the runbook. Attendee emails in the preflight are great — thanks.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com

Attachment: console_lab_runbook.pdf (draft)
From: Emma Li <emma.li@ledgerly.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh@ledgerly.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compact console lab request — availability and headcount

Thanks Logan — Wed Sept 8, 15:00–16:00 PT works best for our exec window. We do need it clipped to 60 minutes exactly.

A couple follow-ups: 
- Backfill: excellent — we have one engineer who might be pulled; 2 hours notice is reasonable.
- For the exercise, temporary tokens are preferable (security org does not want longer-lived service keys). Can you confirm the token lifecycle (expiry) for the session?
- Can you also include a 1-slide "post-session playbook" for devs about next steps and quick links?

I'll accept the seat from the placeholder and update attendees. Please go ahead and send the final invite and runbook; we'll add our internal SOC contact if Irene needs to coordinate token exchange.

Best,
Emma

Attachment: ledgerly-updated-attendees.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@ledgerly.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compact console lab request — Wed Sept 8 confirmed (60m)

Appreciate the quick decision — Wed Sept 8, 15:00–16:00 PT is locked in on our side. A few operational bits from the enablement run: 

- Token lifecycle: we can issue a scoped session token that expires after 4 hours (we'll provide a one-time URL to mint the token during the session). That meets the "temporary token" requirement and avoids long-lived keys. Irene, can you confirm the mint URL and whether we need Ledgerly's SOC contact on the exchange?
- Seat backfill: noted. If someone drops, forward the replacement's full name + email to this thread and we'll add them as "active participant" in the session. Observers don't need tokens.
- Post-session slide: we'll include a 1-slide playbook and a short follow-up doc with links to the console exports and an FAQ.

Logistics: can you share the final attendee list by EOD Tue Sept 1 so we can pre-generate temp tokens for the active seats?

I'll own the API exercise (reduced to a single flow) and will prepare a trimmed runbook.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Customer Enablement, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compact console lab request — token provisioning and SOC contact

Hi all — looping in a short checklist for Ledgerly's SOC team to expedite session tokens: 

1) A single named contact for token handoff + confirmation email (we'll only exchange the mint URL with that address).
2) Final attendee list (full name + email) by EOD Tue Sept 1 — mark any possible backfills.
3) If Ledgerly requires a narrower scope, state the model(s) and routes we should expose (default: console demo + one API route for generation).

Operational notes: the token mint URL will create a 4-hour scoped token and will be time-locked to the session window. We'll only publish the mint URL to the named SOC contact and the session host (Logan/Ben). No long-lived keys will be shared.

Emma — when you have the SOC contact, reply-all with the name and best email and we'll hand off the mint URL.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Infra Security, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
